first_impression.reaction: Typed 'honeymoon planner vs travel agent' on the train. The intro answers it in about three lines: they're just labels, compare the service. Bit of a non-answer, but it's honest and it's fast, which is what I want. Key Takeaways are right there and short. Then I jumped to the comparison table expecting the difference, and both columns are the same questions word for word. That's where I nearly bailed. The FAQ saved it: 'Do we need a travel agent?' gets a straight 'No.'

journey.quote: So compare the service, not the title.
journey.reaction: Okay, that's the answer, in the first paragraph. Not the 'here are five differences' I expected, but I get it. No scrolling needed.

journey.quote: "Honeymoon planner" and "travel agent" are overlapping labels without official definitions, so compare what each business will actually do.
journey.reaction: Clear. Repeats the intro, but if I'd skipped the intro this is all I'd need.

journey.quote: Consumer guarantees, supplier terms, insurance timing and insolvency risk apply whichever label you choose.
journey.reaction: Useful in principle, but 'consumer guarantees' whose? Feels like it's written for a specific country and doesn't say which up top.

journey.section: The same questions, side by side
journey.quote: | Who will we deal with from first call to return? | Who will we deal with from first call to return? | You know who to call, and whether that person changes along the way. |
journey.reaction: Wait, the 'Ask a planner' and 'Ask an agent' columns are identical on every row. On my phone that's a wide table with the same text twice. I get the point (same questions for both) but it looks like a mistake. One column would do.

journey.section: Questions about how they are paid
journey.quote: Do you earn commission from the places you book, and is that shown to us?
journey.reaction: Good, short list. I'd screenshot this one and send it to my fiance.

journey.section: Questions about how they are paid
journey.quote: When money is sent overseas, the provider chooses the exchange rate and charges fees, and the cost depends on how much you send, where you send it and how.
journey.reaction: Now we're on money transfers. That's not what I searched. Scrolled past.

journey.section: Questions about what happens when plans change
journey.quote: As at November 2026, consumer guarantees give you rights if a travel service is delayed or cancelled.
journey.reaction: Dated, nice, I know it's current. But the insurance stuff after this is a lot of reading for something off my question. Skimmed.

journey.quote: Wedded Wonderland is both in one relationship, so you never have to explain your wedding to someone who has not planned it, or your travel to someone who has not moved guests overseas.
journey.reaction: Fine, that's the sales bit and it's clearly labelled. The bullets are tidy. Doesn't tell me what it costs or whether they've done trips like mine.

journey.quote: No. Consumer guarantees apply whether you book directly or through an agent or intermediary.
journey.reaction: Love a one-word answer. This FAQ is the most useful bit on a phone.

journey.quote: Start with two questions: who will we deal with from first call to return, and what will you confirm in writing before we commit?
journey.reaction: Good. Two questions I can actually remember. That's the bookmarkable bit.

unanswered_questions: So is there any practical difference between how a planner and a travel agent usually work, or none at all? (page deliberately avoids generalisations)
How does Wedded Wonderland charge: flat fee, percentage of the trip, or a mix? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Wonderland earn commission from the suppliers it books, and is that disclosed? (deferred business detail)
Roughly what does honeymoon planning cost with you? (deferred business detail: page gives no figures)
Is there a real honeymoon you've planned that I can look at? (deferred business detail)
Are there any perks for booking through you, like upgrades or extras? (deferred business detail)
Do you hold insolvency cover, since the page tells me to ask? (deferred business detail)
Do you work with couples who don't live in Australia? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: | Ask a planner | Ask an agent | Why it matters |
turn_offs_found.why: The headings promise a comparison but every row repeats the same question in both columns. On a phone that's a wide table of duplicated text, and it reads like an error rather than a point being made.

turn_offs_found.quote: When money is sent overseas, the provider chooses the exchange rate and charges fees, and the cost depends on how much you send, where you send it and how.
turn_offs_found.why: Drifts off my question. I came to compare planners and agents, not to learn about exchange rates. More scrolling for a phone reader.

would_share_with: My fiance, the 'Questions about how they are paid' list and the two first questions from the FAQ, as a checklist before we talk to anyone

cta_reaction.quote: To start, [meet your Wedded Advisor through Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=honeymoon-planner-vs-travel-agent&utm_content=secondary).
cta_reaction.why: I don't know this brand and I came for a quick answer. The page earned a bookmark, not an enquiry. Maybe later if I'm actually choosing someone.

top_3_changes: Collapse the side-by-side table to one 'Ask either of them' column plus 'Why it matters', or retitle it so it's obvious the identical columns are deliberate. Right now it looks like a copy-paste error on mobile.
Say once, near the top, that the rights and insurance points are for Australian couples, so the 'consumer guarantees' takeaway isn't confusing for anyone searching from elsewhere.
Trim or fold the money-transfer and insurance detail into a short checklist so phone readers get back to the planner vs agent question faster.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Priya (search visitor): intro, Key Takeaways, one section and FAQ, skimmed on a phone, flagged structure issues
No invented brand facts; fee model, commissions, ranges, real honeymoons, perks and proof placed in unanswered_questions as deferred, not must-fix
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
Absence of figures and generalisations not penalised in top_3_changes; changes are structural only

open_questions.question: Is the duplicated planner/agent table intentional? If so, should it be reduced to a single column to avoid looking like an error on mobile?

assumptions: Priya arrived from a Google search for 'honeymoon planner vs travel agent' on her phone, does not know the brand and is not based in Australia, so relevance is 3 and enquiry likelihood is 1.
Deferred business details (fee model, commissions, ranges, real honeymoons, perks, proof) are not penalised and are listed as unanswered questions only.
The 3-minute budget covered the intro, Key Takeaways, the comparison table, the paid-questions list, a skim of the changes and insurance sections, the Wedded Wonderland section and the FAQ.
